newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA COSATU SOFTENS LABOUR BILL STANCE - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA COSATU SOFTENS LABOUR BILL STANCE - PAPER.

text.p: The Congress of South African (Cosatu) has decided to soften its previous uncompromising position on a new employment bill, opening the way for a resumption of talks with government and business, Business Day newspaper said on Thursday.

However, it said that the country's biggest labour union would still go ahead from Monday with a programme of mass action, announced last month in defence of its demands regarding the new Conditions of Employment Bill.
Business, in response to Cosatu's rethink on the bill, had indicated that it would be prepared to review its tough position. Agreement would ensure the tabling of the bill in parliament this year.

The paper quoted sources as saying delegates were forced to rethink Cosatu's position in the face of alliance partner, the African National Congress (ANC) national executive committee's decision to endorse the bill as it stood.

Sam Shilowa, general secretary of Cosatu, said leadership had been mandated to "explore possibilities of a settlement with the ANC". The union, however, cautioned that it was not signalling a compromise on core demands.

A willingness to review positions on a 40-hour working week, four months paid maternity leave, child labour age limit and variation of standards through private agreements could lead to agreement with the ANC, the paper said.
There was also heated debate on whether the union, which has nearly two million members, could risk the bill not being tabled, a move threatened by Labour Minister Tito Mboweni.
Cosatu said last month it planned two full-day national strikes plus a programme of regional action in defence of its demands regarding new labour legislation.
The programme kicks off with a nationwide one-hour work stoppage on Monday between 10.00 a.m. and 11.00 a.m. (0800-0900 GMT).
The labour federation has already held a one-day national stoppage last month to drive home its claims.
